title: Issue status does not establish fix coverage or novelty
applies_when: A source-audit lead resembles an open or closed issue, a merged fix to a sibling method, a multi-case report, or a prior no-op restriction whose return-value contract was not checked.
lesson: Read the issue body, latest discussion and linked patch before setup or deciding whether a finding is new or fixed. An open issue can already have a reporter-confirmed repair: Megatron #8179's comments point to #7582 and report that the original tied-weight reproducer passed. Preserve author ownership, not a competing fix based only on the initial body. Separate three questions: is the behavior reproducible now, was this exact case already reported, and did the accepted patch address it? A PR can explicitly leave a known streaming limitation out of scope: a new reproduction does not make that case novel or newly introduced. AnyIO #1081 also reports negative receive_exactly, beyond the receive API in its title; merged #1191's max_bytes validation does not prove exact-read coverage. Return to that report rather than claiming fresh discovery. Similarly, a maintainer's prohibition on moving a stream position does not require an accepted no-op seek to return None: check the actual return contract and consumer separately. An existing repair or passing characterization test is not evidence that every remaining behavior was deliberately requested. Record scoped advice without suppressing the whole file or rewriting raw model answers.
avoid_when: Reporter-confirmed repair is not our independent native qualification, proof of merge or all-case support. A current native failure does not prove novelty, intended behavior or maintainer acceptance. Do not copy a sibling API's positive-size constraint: zero-length exact reads can differ from bounded receive. Preserve streaming restrictions when repairing no-op returns; a synchronous BufferedReader reproduction does not prove async zip/tar compatibility or justify random access. These are scoped counterexamples, not a measured Scout conversion/miss-rate improvement or a universal rule to reopen closed issues.

evidence.note: The closed report explicitly includes negative and zero receive_exactly cases and reproducer tests, beyond the receive(max_bytes) API named in its title. It establishes prior reporting, not the final contract for every case.
The merged follow-on describes validation of max_bytes in ByteReceiveStream.receive implementations. Its closure of #1081 alone does not establish receive_exactly coverage.

Pinned source still uses buffer[:nbytes] when remaining <= 0, with no negative-nbytes guard. This is scoped current-source evidence, not proof that the behavior is supported, novel or accepted for repair.
The maintainer asks that async/streaming files not be seekable. This addresses position-changing seeks, not an explicit requirement that permitted no-op calls return None.
After merged #2214, both HTTP stream classes still return None from accepted no-op seeks. Same-function repair history does not remove this distinct return-value behavior.

Follow-up returns current offsets without enabling random access. Exact-source loopback BufferedReader raises TypeError before and returns integer positions after; 110 official HTTP cases pass. Observed merged on 2026-10-18 (merge 29fa21219ea457eb83f36ee838a3744ec87c697a): scoped maintainer acceptance, not proof of all CI passing, async archive compatibility or measured selector utility.

The open issue's Oct14 discussion points to PR7582; the reporter confirms the original tied-weight reproduction completes two iterations, validation and test. This is reported evidence, not our execution or a merge verdict.

Author-owned OneToOne.update one-shot-iterator repair. Linux CPython3.12 head e5f2c7b: 50 focused passes; unchanged 4e5faa3 with identical tests: 43 passes/7 failures, other outcomes unchanged. Not full tox/OS coverage or maintainer acceptance; no competing repair.

Prior open PR reports and repairs CachedFunction ignoring scoped=True; its head is not independently qualified here. Current main can retain the bug while review waits. A stale search snapshot or empty collected list is not novelty evidence.

Author-owned BarrelList repair covers clipped bounds, empty inputs and stepped/reverse deletion. Windows validation is author-reported; the head was inspected, not independently qualified here. A current-base failure is not our new discovery.
Current-base del_slice still raises IndexError on clipped/empty deletion while PR549 waits. Read that repair; unrelated BarrelList methods remain separate, and maintainer acceptance is unproven.

OneToOne.update consumes a pair before materializing the remaining iterator; PR523 already covers it. Copy, serialization and other update subcases need separate contract, duplicate and native checks, not a whole-module exclusion.
CachedFunction omits scoped from key construction while PR498 exists. Source affinity exposes prior work, not an automatic negative label, file exclusion or measured discovery improvement.
Existing author repair covers oversized Bits right shifts producing negative widths. Author-reported tests are not our qualification.
The current __rshift__ subtracts width unchecked while PR495 already covers it. Read that repair; other Bits contracts remain separate.
Existing author repair rejects nonempty unparseable duration text but preserves blank-input compatibility. Head not independently tested here.
parse_timedelta can still return zero on invalid text while PR548 waits. Different repeated-unit behavior has separate PR583.

The merged PR body explicitly acknowledges raw ReadTimeout after the first streamed token and leaves it out of scope. This is a known streaming limitation, not proof it is desirable or permanently rejected. Do not announce a new regression or unsolicited competing repair.

_inner_post catches httpx2 timeouts around response setup/nonstream reads but returns a lazy iterator for streams. Current source reproduces the already-declared gap; other inference paths still need independent review.
